blocks.content: **What you will learn:** Drilldown investigates by clicking, not by writing queries. You'll pick a kind of data, narrow to one metric, and see where to narrow further.
First, pick a kind of data:
Click **Drilldown** in the main menu. Each kind of data gets its own door: numbers, text records, request maps, and resource use.
Click **Metrics**, the numbers recorded over time. Every metric appears as a chart, before you ask for anything.
You picked a kind of data, and Drilldown showed everything it has. No query written.
Next, narrow the view down to one thing:
Click **Select** on the first metric. The view narrows to that one metric, broken down by its labels.
blocks.tooltip: One click narrows from everything to one thing. The breakdown that opens splits it further, one chart per label.

blocks.content: This is a **filter**: pick a label and a value, and every chart narrows to match. Clicking filters is the whole workflow.
blocks.tooltip: Each pick narrows the result. Stack a few and you've cornered the problem, without writing a query.

blocks.content: One problem leaves marks in more than one kind of data. **Related logs** hops from these numbers to the matching text records.
blocks.tooltip: The same investigation can jump between kinds of data: a spike in the numbers often has a matching error line in the text.

blocks.content: **What you have learned:** Drilldown starts from everything and narrows with clicks: pick a kind of data, pick one thing, filter by labels. The related tabs carry the same investigation into other kinds of data.
